claims.claim: Arena provisions source-backed MCP servers via MCPSources, named factories that open an MCP endpoint at a lifecycle boundary and tear it down when the boundary closes
Source-backed MCP is the third MCP transport, alongside stdio (command) and static HTTP+SSE (url)
Link to /arena/how-to/agents/test-mcp-tools/ for static servers
Config path spec.mcp_servers is a list of entries under the arena spec
name is the registry key and is used in qualified tool names
source names a registered MCPSource (example docker)
scope field selects when the source opens and closes
source_args is an opaque map handed to the source's Open(); schema is per source
source is the name of an MCPSource registered in the running binary
scope accepts one of run, scenario, session
source_args is a free-form map passed to the source's Open()
An entry needs a name and sets exactly one of source, url and command; a source entry needs a scope of run, scenario or session; otherwise the config fails to load in validate and run
scope run opens once at arena startup and closes at arena shutdown
scope scenario opens at each scenario start and closes at each scenario end
scope session opens for each repetition (each executeRun) and closes after that repetition's assertions
Inner scopes close before outer scopes
Closer errors are logged as warnings and never fail the parent scope
If Open() fails partway through a scope's entries, already-opened entries in that scope are torn down before the error propagates
source_args is templated against each scenario's variables block before the source sees it
Only {{scenario.<key>}} substitution is supported, with no fallbacks or expressions
Scenario spec has a variables block containing repo and branch keys in the example
source_args.repo may be set to the template {{scenario.repo}}
source_args.branch may be set to the template {{scenario.branch}}
Each session opens a fresh container with the scenario's repo cloned into /workspace
When Open() returns, Arena registers the resulting URL and headers in the runtime MCP registry under the entry's name
Arena calls tools/list against the server after Open() returns
Each discovered tool is registered as a ToolDescriptor in the tools registry
Source-backed tools are registered under their raw MCP name, not the mcp__server__tool form
MCPExecutor looks up the owning server via the registry's tool index, regardless of namespace
Tools are referenced by name in the prompt config allowed_tools field
A provider that declares a capabilities list must include tools in it for tool calls to work
A prompt only reaches tools named in allowed_tools; no entry means no tools
Tool results appear in messages with a real tool role, not as tool-shaped text in content
allowed_tools example list contains Read, Edit, Bash, run_tests
If two source-backed servers expose tools with the same name, the second registration overwrites the first
Stdio and url MCP entries give namespaced isolation (mcp__server__tool)
PromptArena registers a docker source automatically
The docker source shells out to the local docker CLI to run, exec and stop the container
image is a required string arg; the container must expose an MCP HTTP+SSE server on port 8080
repo is optional; when set, the source runs docker exec <cid> git clone [--branch <branch>] <repo> /workspace after start
branch is optional, defaults to the repo default branch, and is ignored when repo is empty
env is a map passed via docker -e; numbers and booleans are formatted as text and list or map values fail the open
mounts is a list of objects with source, target, readonly, mode and when; bind mounts are passed to docker run -v and copy mounts are put in with docker cp
ports is a list of ints; each is published to a free host port; 8080 is rejected
network is passed to --network; none and host are rejected
cpus is passed to --cpus; default is unlimited
memory is passed to --memory; default is unlimited
The source picks a free local port and publishes container port 8080 to it
The source polls http://localhost:<port>/sse until it returns 2xx with a 20 second budget
The source returns the /sse URL (http://localhost:<port>/sse) as the server's endpoint
On Close() the container is stopped and removed
Ports listed under ports are published and exposed to session hooks as sandbox_ports in event metadata
Event metadata also carries sandbox_containers next to sandbox_ports
Example config uses ports [3000], cpus 2 and memory 2g
Metadata key sandbox_containers maps the source name to a container id
Metadata key sandbox_ports maps the source name to a map of container port to http://localhost:<port>
A session_end hook event exists and can use the sandbox_ports mapping
The built-in docker source runs git clone unauthenticated
Link to https://github.com/AltairaLabs/promptarena/v2/tree/main/examples/codegen-sandbox
The example provisions ghcr.io/altairalabs/codegen-sandbox:latest per session
The example mounts skills/codegen read-only at /skills/codegen inside the container
The example's mock-LLM scenario seeds a buggy Go module via Bash, reads and edits the file, and verifies via run_tests
go build -o bin/promptarena ./arena/cmd/promptarena builds the binary
promptarena run accepts --ci and --format markdown
The run writes examples/codegen-sandbox/out/results.md
promptarena run accepts --mock-provider and runs against canned LLM responses
A tool_exec check exists and invokes a registered tool at session end, asserting the call succeeded
Codegen sandboxes typically expose run_tests, run_lint and run_typecheck
tool_exec reads structured success or failure from tool results
A spec.scenarios list entry takes a file key
Scenario apiVersion is promptkit.altairalabs.ai/v1alpha1 and kind is Scenario
Scenario spec.id and metadata.name are fields; spec.task_type is codegen-agent in the example
Scenario spec.turns entries take role and content
Scenario spec.conversation_assertions entries take type, params and message
conversation_assertions type tool_exec takes params.tool
A session-scoped MCP source keeps the container alive across the agent's tool calls and the tool_exec gate call
The gate runs run_tests one more time after the agent declares done
Arena adds a read-only mount to source_args.mounts for each skill source with a path; a directory of skills mounts each skill inside it
A skill directory mounts at /skills/<name>, where name is the source's name or the directory base name
Skill mount entries are readonly true
The docker source translates each mount entry into a -v <src>:<tgt>:ro flag on docker run
Scripts shipped with a skill are runnable via Bash /skills/<name>/scripts/<script>
Config load fails with unknown source "X" when the named source is not registered, and the error lists the registered names
Error container not healthy: health timeout after 20s occurs when the image is not serving HTTP+SSE on 8080 or /sse returns non-2xx
Error tool <name> validation error (args_invalid) occurs when args do not match the MCP input schema
Error tool not found: <name> occurs after a successful Open when tools/list returned nothing or two servers collided
Link to /arena/reference/config-schema/#mcp_servers anchor
Link to /arena/how-to/scenarios/write-scenarios/ for the variables block
Link to https://promptkit.altairalabs.ai/runtime/how-to/integrate-mcp/ for the low-level MCP registry API
Mounts set on the entry are kept and come first; a skill mount whose target a user mount uses is dropped
Inline skills get no mount
Each mounts entry takes source and target, plus optional readonly, mode and when; any other key is rejected
mount source is relative to the directory holding the arena config, must exist and must stay inside it after following symlinks
{{scenario.<variable>}} in a mount source is replaced from the scenario's variables
mount target must be an absolute container path and each target may appear once
readonly defaults to true, mode to bind, when to start
mode: copy puts files in with docker cp and gives them to the container's own user so the agent can edit them without changing host files
when: eval requires mode: copy and scope: session
when: eval files are copied in after the agent's last turn and before conversation-level assertions and pack evals run
promptarena validate checks every mount, once per scenario when source uses a scenario variable
A skill mount whose target a user mount also uses fails the open with an error naming the target
bind mounts go to docker run -v; copy mounts with when: start are copied in after the container starts
